name: Vesting, Repurchase, and Acceleration

positioning.oneLineSummary: Models service vesting, prior credit, leaver repurchase, pool return, and change-of-control acceleration by holder and event.
positioning.productLabel: Vesting and Acceleration Lens — based on Feld and Mendelson's public Venture Deals materials
notAClaimOf: four years and one cliff being a universal default
vesting being only an employee-compensation term
single or double trigger being universally preferable

attribution.display: Based on Brad Feld and Jason Mendelson's public vesting materials

neutralParaphrase: For each founder, employee, director, and advisor grant, track service start, vesting schedule, prior credit, cliff, repurchase right and price, termination treatment, pool return, and change-of-control acceleration. Compare retention, ownership, and acquisition effects across actual event states rather than applying a market-default schedule.

locator.value: Service vesting, founder credit, repurchase, options returning to pool, and single/double-trigger acceleration
Chapter 5: vesting and exercise period; Chapter 19: employment, 409A, 83(b), and founders' stock

requiredConditions: Every grant and founder holding has an executed document and service-start date.
Vesting, repurchase, termination, acceleration, and exercise rules are holder-specific.
Acquisition and termination states are defined separately.
Tax, 409A, 83(b), employment, and enforceability questions go to counsel.

requiredEvidence.description: Holder, instrument, shares, grant date, service start, cliff, cadence, duration, prior credit, and current vested balance.
Termination definitions, repurchase right, price, exercise period, forfeiture, and pool-return rules.
Single/double trigger, covered events, termination window, good-reason definition, assumption, substitution, and acceleration amount.

decisionQuestions: How much of each holder's equity is vested today and at each milestone?
What happens on voluntary departure, termination, death/disability, or cause?
Who may repurchase unvested shares, at what price, and by when?
Does unvested equity return to the pool?
What acquisition and termination events trigger acceleration?
How do retention, buyer integration, and remaining-holder ownership change?
positiveSignals: All grants reconcile to the equity ledger.
Founder prior service and future retention are explicitly balanced.
Leaver and repurchase rules are unambiguous.
Acceleration triggers and amounts are consistent across documents.
Acquisition states show employee, founder, buyer, and pool effects.
redFlags: A default schedule is assumed without grant documents.
Founder stock is treated as fully owned despite repurchase rights.
Exercise deadlines or option expiration are omitted.
The system provides tax or employment-law advice.
disconfirmingEvidence: Board approvals or grant records conflict with the cap table.
An employment agreement overrides plan language.
A change-of-control event does not meet the contractual definition.
Repurchase or exercise windows have expired.
contraindications: Do not apply a market-standard schedule as company fact.
Do not calculate without holder-level documents.
Do not provide tax, employment, or enforceability conclusions.
Do not let the LLM calculate vested balances.

instructions: Reconcile grants and founder holdings to legal records.
Parse service, cliff, cadence, credit, leaver, repurchase, exercise, and acceleration rules.
Run current, milestone, termination, and acquisition states.
Show holder and pool ownership changes.
Route tax, employment, and legal issues to counsel.

sourceReliability.low: Only cap-table shares or a verbal schedule are known.
sourceReliability.medium: Core grants exist but employment or transaction terms are incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: Grant, plan, ledger, employment, board, and transaction documents reconcile.

evidenceStrength.medium: Current vesting is reproducible but a leaver or acquisition state is ambiguous.
evidenceStrength.high: Every holder and state is deterministic.

evidenceCoverage.medium: Schedules and grants are covered but leaver, exercise, or acceleration is partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Schedules, credit, leaver, repurchase, exercise, acceleration, pool, and all holders are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.medium: Service equity exists with custom jurisdictional terms.
applicabilityConfidence.high: All grant and event terms are explicit.

judgmentConfidence.low: Only document gaps can be listed.
judgmentConfidence.medium: Current balances and a bounded event range are usable.
judgmentConfidence.high: Retention and ownership effects are reproducible.

promotionRequirements: Golden-case tests for holder and acquisition states.
Complete fourth-edition vesting and legal chapter review.
empiricalQualifications: Vesting conventions vary by geography, role, stage, and negotiation.
Retention effects depend on compensation and team context beyond documents.
Acquisition acceleration can affect buyer willingness and employee incentives.

rights.notes: Historical public conventions are not product defaults; exact outcomes require executed documents.

openIssues: Define vesting event schema and time-zone/date policy.
